text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Austrian newspapers.
- Conservative People's party chief Wolfgang Schuessel demands Austrian interests in Creditanstalt be protected. Going public is a very possible alternative to a sale.
- Germany's Allianz has denied any interest in buying Creditanstalt.
- Austrians, compared to 19 other OECD members, go to hospital the most, a study says.
- Finance Minister Viktor Klima has presented plans for Austria's budget to the year 2000. The deficit is to be reduced to 58.5 percent of GDP.

- Austrian retail sales rose 3.2 percent to 239.5 billion schillings in the first half of 1996 compared to the previous year. Wholesales however went down 3.2 percent to 439.8 billion schillings in the same time.
- Sales in mineral water went down 21 and 15 percent respectively in July and August. For 1996 sales are expected to be down by four percent.
- Finance Minister Viktor Klima hopes to boost the state's coffers by 2000 through selling the government's stakes in Austria Tabak and banks.
- The consortium around EA-Generali only wants to buy half of the government's stake in Creditanstalt, the rest is to be sold through the stock exchange.
- Austria's export industry is losing ground in Hungary. Exports to the neighbouring country have fallen 12.2 percent to 741.5 million schillings in the first half of 1996.
- Klima says a new call for bids for Creditanstalt is quite likely, however a sale of the government's stake through the stock exchange is a possibility too.
